annotations.title: Enforcement capacity from sourced protocol parameters (paid)

description: Paid: 2 credits ($2.00) per answered call, charged once and only after a non-empty answer is computed; an unavailable answer, a refusal or an error costs nothing. Send your API key in the X-API-Key header or as api_key. Each call is a new answer and a new charge (no idempotency key). Computes the left-hand side of Theorem 1 in Qazi (2026, arXiv:2608.12576), the enforcement capacity p * (lambda*S + delta*min Phi): the largest per-audit deterrence ratio a network's slashing and probation can support, in the network's stake unit. Inputs are the network's published protocol parameters (stake per provider, slash fraction, audit probability, probation ladder, hardware-identity binding), each returned with the URL it was read from and the date it was last confirmed there; unsourced stake or slash parameters are refused, never defaulted, and so is one not re-confirmed within 60 days. Where a network publishes no audit probability, p = 1 is used and the figure is labelled an upper bound (capacity_upper_bound_p1); a slash fraction published only as a recommended default is labelled so and its range is reported. Structural screens (deviations that cannot be detected, missing identity binding) are reported. A ceiling, not a verdict: the cheating gain it would have to exceed is private, so no incentive-compatibility answer is given. Networks without sourced parameters are answered unavailable and not charged.
